name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) is a large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research. The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox and consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish). The dataset also includes Language Models (LM) and baseline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models for all languages.
license: Public domain (LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data released in the public domain)
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: English, German, Dutch, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Polish
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 2020.
rai:dataCollection: Audio data was collected from LibriVox audiobooks using LibriLight open source library tools. Text sources for audiobooks were downloaded from multiple domains including gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org. For non-English languages, manual approaches were also used including copying text from browsers, extracting text from PDF/EPUB books using pdftotext, and writing HTML parsers for popular domains. Audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models. Pseudo labels were generated via beam-search decoding with a 4-gram language model. Transcripts were retrieved by matching pseudo-labels to source book text using TF-IDF similarity and Smith-Waterman alignment.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Text sources for some audiobooks were missing due to invalid links or pages redirecting to incorrect pages. For audiobooks with invalid links, manual searches were conducted to find alternate sources. For example, text sources from spiegel.de (accounting for 1/3 of German audio data) were being redirected to invalid pages, but alternate sources were found from projekt-gutenberg.de and zeno.org.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks (read audiobooks in the public domain) and corresponding text sources from Project Gutenberg and other online sources (gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, hathitrust.org, spiegel.de, projekt-gutenberg.de, zeno.org). The dataset covers 8 languages: English, German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, and Polish.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: Numbers in matched text were replaced with corresponding aligned words from pseudo labels to handle ambiguous number pronunciations. For hyphens and apostrophes, heuristics were used to replace rare word forms (words appearing in fewer than a threshold number of distinct books) with normalized forms.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Audio was segmented into 10-20 second segments by finding the longest silence duration within the 10-20 second range and splitting at the midpoint of the silence chunk. If no silence frames were found between 10-20 seconds, the audio was split at the 20-second mark. Candidate transcripts with WER greater than 40% between the candidate transcript and pseudo label were filtered out. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or duplicate versions were removed. Speakers were split into train, development, and test sets with no speaker overlap, balanced by gender and duration.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), removal of end-of-line hyphens, and filtering of characters outside the valid unicode range for each language's orthography. Audio segmentation was performed using trained acoustic models with TDS Convolutions and ASG loss. Transcript retrieval used TF-IDF similarity on bigrams with Smith-Waterman alignment (matching score 2, substitution/insertion/deletion score -1). Candidate transcripts with WER >40% were filtered. For language model data, books with title edit distance less than 2 from dev/test books were removed, and books sharing more than 1% of 5-grams with dev/test sets were also removed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Development and test set transcripts were verified by human transcribers who listened to audio files while reviewing transcripts and corrected clear and obvious errors. Human transcribers were instructed to only correct clear and obvious errors to avoid introducing bias. Gender labels for all speakers were assigned using a trained SVM gender classifier with RBF kernel.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcripts (GT) and human-rated transcripts (HRT) was measured for dev and test sets across all languages. Error rates ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev). The gender classifier achieved 95% accuracy on LibriSpeech speakers, 96% on Dutch speakers, and 94% on Polish speakers.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SVM gender classifier with RBF kernel trained on 1172 speakers from LibriSpeech train-clean-100 and train-clean-360 subsets; wav2letter@anywhere framework for streaming inference; TDS Convolution acoustic models with ASG loss for audio segmentation and pseudo-label generation; KenLM toolkit for 3-gram and 5-gram language models; pdftotext for extracting text from PDF/EPUB books
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is freely available at http://www.openslr.org. Pretrained models and recipes are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/wav2letter. No explicit versioning or deprecation policy is described.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker gender information is included in the dataset. The in-house training data used for acoustic models consists of videos publicly shared by users, which is completely de-identified.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to open new avenues in ASR and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research by providing a large, freely available multilingual speech corpus. It aims to promote open research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR, and can be used to extend LibriTTS for multilingual TTS research.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks, which may not represent conversational or spontaneous speech. English is heavily dominant compared to other languages (44.5K hours vs. ~6K hours total for 7 other languages). The gender classifier used to label speakers may introduce errors (accuracy ranges from 94-96%). Development and test sets are intentionally chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions for English.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to read speech from audiobooks and may not generalize to conversational or spontaneous speech. Polish has a high OOV rate of 13.39% in the language model, which negatively impacts ASR performance with LM decoding. Some audiobooks could not be included due to missing or invalid text source links. The dataset covers only 8 languages despite LibriVox having data in many more languages.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and training, Text-To-Speech (TTS) research, multilingual speech research, and low-resource ASR benchmarking (via limited supervision train sets of 10 hours, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets). Baseline ASR models and language models are provided for all 8 languages.
